# White sugar

<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as white sugar

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-white-sugar" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-white-sugar-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of white sugar, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤4</td><td>≤20</td><td>20–100 (bounded)</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤4</td><td>≤20</td><td>20–100 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>122 reference units; 7 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>100</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>FDA Total Diet Study</td><td>3</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Alcívar et al. 2024</td><td>4</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Grembecka et al. 2012</td><td>3</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Spungen et al. 2024</td><td>1</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Stojanović et al. 2021</td><td>1</td><td>14%</td></tr><tr><td>Topraksever 2026</td><td>10</td><td>14%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for white sugar, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>7 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" data-no-cite-meta>FDA Total Diet Study</a></li><li><a href="../sources/alcivar2024-ecuador-sugarcane-panela-cadmium-lead" class="internal" data-slug="sources/alcivar2024-ecuador-sugarcane-panela-cadmium-lead" data-no-cite-meta>Alcívar et al. 2024</a></li><li><a href="../sources/grembecka2012-poland-confectionery-sugar-cocoa-chocolate-minerals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/grembecka2012-poland-confectionery-sugar-cocoa-chocolate-minerals" data-no-cite-meta>Grembecka et al. 2012</a></li><li><a href="../sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium" class="internal" data-slug="sources/spungen2024-fda-tds-infant-lead-cadmium" data-no-cite-meta>Spungen et al. 2024</a></li><li><a href="../sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/stojanovic2021-serbia-canned-meat-tinplate-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Stojanović et al. 2021</a></li><li><a href="../sources/topraksever2026-turkish-red-sugar-elements-icpms" class="internal" data-slug="sources/topraksever2026-turkish-red-sugar-elements-icpms" data-no-cite-meta>Topraksever 2026</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>3</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for white sugar, as sold on a basis not stated by the source basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach white sugar

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach white sugar comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. White sugar, as sold from commercial sample S4 had chromium higher at 227 µg/kg, against 4.63 µg/kg for commercial sample S2 in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/topraksever2026-turkish-red-sugar-elements-icpms|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Topraksever N · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/topraksever2026-turkish-red-sugar-elements-icpms">Multi-Element Characterization and Sustainability Assessment of Traditional Turkish Red Sugar Using Deep Eutectic Solvent Extraction and ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 2026, 15, 3719</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/topraksever2026-turkish-red-sugar-elements-icpms">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.



<a id="ranges-by-source-region-and-variety"></a>
## Which forms and regions measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>
<a id="how-do-concentrations-vary-by-origin-growing-conditions-variety-and-harvest-period"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-distinguishes-within-lot-between-lot-supplier-and-production-system-variation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-015"></a>
<a id="which-comparisons-support-a-sourcing-decision-and-where-would-geographic-or-supplier-generalization-be-unjustified"></a>

The HMI reference for lead in white sugar, as sold pools 122 subgroup units from 7 sampling families, with a median of below 20 µg/kg and a middle half spanning below 4 (lower quartile) and between 20 and 100 µg/kg (upper quartile).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span <summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in white sugar?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, methylmercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, Ba, Ca, K, Mg, Sr and Tl in white sugar, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/alcivar2024-ecuador-sugarcane-panela-cadmium-lead|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Alcívar M, Vinueza E, Pernía B, Álvarez-Montero X, Gallardo A · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-white-sugar" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-white-sugar" data-question="How do heavy metals get into white sugar?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into white sugar?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, white sugar from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than white sugar from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/topraksever2026-turkish-red-sugar-elements-icpms|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Topraksever N · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/topraksever2026-turkish-red-sugar-elements-icpms">Multi-Element Characterization and Sustainability Assessment of Traditional Turkish Red Sugar Using Deep Eutectic Solvent Extraction and ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 2026, 15, 3719</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/topraksever2026-turkish-red-sugar-elements-icpms">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> White sugar, as sold from commercial sample S1 had lead higher at 919 µg/kg, against 426 µg/kg for commercial sample S1 in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/topraksever2026-turkish-red-sugar-elements-icpms|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Topraksever N · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/topraksever2026-turkish-red-sugar-elements-icpms">Multi-Element Characterization and Sustainability Assessment of Traditional Turkish Red Sugar Using Deep Eutectic Solvent Extraction and ICP-MS</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 2026, 15, 3719</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/topraksever2026-turkish-red-sugar-elements-icpms">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-white-sugar" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-white-sugar" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in white sugar?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in white sugar?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, white sugar, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (5.3 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (82 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (0.2 µg/kg) and the highest in EMRO (23 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-white-sugar-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-white-sugar-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in white sugar is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in white sugar is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 14 results from 5 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span
